- If sentiment is positive (≥0.33) in recent history, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% for next period.
- If model shows gradual upward trend (e.g., +0.1–0.3 per day) but true outcome spikes sharply, reduce forecast slope after spike; avoid overcommitting to continuation.
- When true outcome exceeds model by >2% for 2+ consecutive days, apply mean reversion bias: next forecast = previous + 0.5–1.0% of recent 7-day average deviation.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.00) and model is flat or slightly rising, expect downward correction; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day until sentiment turns.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period spikes (especially after 20–25 days); add 0.5–1.5% buffer to final 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- If model forecast is flat or slightly declining but true outcome rises >1.5% from 18-day average, consider “lag correction”: forecast = true outcome - 0.5–1.0% of 18-day average deviation.
